answer: Resonance-priced coordination lanes: Each agent pays a fee set by how many new peers it contacts per epoch, so broad reach costs more than deep use. An attacker's clones must each buy lane access at the current clearing price, which climbs as distinct identities crowd the same horizon. Honest agents reach a natural zenith of cheap local coordination while clone farms hit rising marginal costs per fake identity. A shared haven of low-fee lanes exists only for agents whose contact graph overlaps already-paid peers, forcing attackers to subsidize real social density.
